messages:
maria: Heads up — nightly evals for quantized-13B on commit d9f4b2 show a spike in timeouts and nondet failures on the reasoning prompt set. Failure rate jumped from 1.2% to ~12% last night.
cheng: Ugh. Any error patterns? timeouts vs bad generations?
maria: Mostly timeouts, but when it finishes outputs are slightly different run-to-run. Logs show worker process OOM-ish hangs then long tail.
sam: Could be the new temp file change from last week? We switched the harness to write tokenized prompts to NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) before sending to workers. Possible fd/handle leak under heavy parallelism.
emily: I saw something similar in infra last month where open file descriptors hit ulimit and worker fds got stuck. ops-bot reported a burst of restarts around 03:12 UTC.
ops-bot: 03:12:24 - eval-worker-7 restarted (OOMKilled) ; 03:12:31 - eval-worker-3 restarted (OOMKilled) ; rolling restarts 03:12-03:18
ben: Can you paste a short log snippet? also, which python/stdlib are the runners on?
maria: Log snippet (truncated):
```
2026-03-19T03:11:59Z eval-worker-7 INFO starting batch 124
2026-03-19T03:12:03Z eval-worker-7 ERROR write /tmp/eval_token_XXXX: [Errno 24] Too many open files
2026-03-19T03:12:07Z eval-worker-7 WARN worker hung for >120s
2026-03-19T03:12:24Z eval-worker-7 CRIT process killed (OOMKilled)
```
maria: Runners are on ubuntu-22.04 images, python 3.10, kernel 5.15. We recently rolled a tiny harness change from @cheng that altered tempfile behavior.
cheng: That was to avoid NamedTemporaryFile on Windows; we used delete=False to be safe. I did not consider ulimits under heavy parallel local procs. :facepalm:
sam: Quick repro: spawn 200 parallel tokenizations that write tempfiles, run `ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd | wc -l` you'll see many open fds until GC/deletion happens.
emily: Two follow-ups: 1) does the quantized tokenizer flush caches to disk? 2) do we spawn subprocess workers with inherit_fds=true?
ben: tokenizer writes mmap-backed files for quantized vocab caches in some code paths. That plus tempfiles will push fd usage up.
cheng: I can revert the tempfile change to use TemporaryDirectory + explicit close/delete in the worker process. Proposal: create temp dir per batch and clean up at worker exit. Will open PR.
maria: For short-term mitigation, can infra increase NOFILE limit for eval pool and restart workers? ops-bot flagged restarts but we need higher threshold.
ops-bot: I can bump system ulimit to 65k for eval nodes and roll new autoscaled instances. Want me to proceed?
maria: Yes, please. Also let's kick off a 1000-sample subset run with the reverted tempfile handling and monitor 2 cycles.
dev-bot: CI: run/eval-harness-tests passed on d9f4b2 (small unit tests) — note: unit tests don't exercise heavy parallel tokenization.
ben: Also add quick deterministic-seed test: run 5 identical evals in a row and diff outputs. If RNG/state leak, we'll catch it.
sam: FYI, Python 3.11 changed some GC timings which could affect when temp files are closed. Worth validating on py3.11 image too.
emily: I'll add a short postmortem checklist: 1) revert tempfile change in harness (PR) 2) increase NOFILE on eval nodes 3) add fd-leak unit test 4) run 3-nightly sanity passes before declaring fixed.
maria: Thanks — assigning follow-ups: @cheng PR, @ops-bot bump NOFILE, @ben add fd test, @emily add checklist. I'll monitor the next nightly and report back. :thumbsup:
